messages:
maya: quick heads-up — I'm prototyping a keyboard-first 'quick grant' in the console (press 'g' when selecting a principal). Idea is one-tap grants for common role presets. question: any concerns about routing/quota side-effects if grants are applied too eagerly? :thinking:
sam: fwiw we already have customers hitting weird routing fallbacks when roles get a route-level entitlement unexpectedly. quick grant must run the same preflight checks as full UI. at minimum call the simulate API and write an audit before applying. :+1:
li: agree with sam. also show an "effective changes" preview inline — small chart: which routes/capacities this principal can now touch. otherwise ops teams freak out.
jordan: keyboard shortcuts are great but we should gate by enterprise flags. some orgs require approval for any role that can change routing policies (e.g. role contains `route_admin` scope). so quick-grant should detect sensitive scopes and open the full modal.
maya: good call. sensitive-scope gating idea: maintain a small list of scopes that force the modal. default list lives in console config + server-side guard. anyone worried about latency making shortcut feel slow?
nora: latency will matter. if simulate + audit + apply is sequential it might take 800ms+. we can optimistically update UI and correct on failure but must show clear rollback UX. also, telemetry event shape needs to capture whether the grant was quick vs modal and whether it triggered sensitive-scope flow.
sam: telemetry ask: include fields {flow: quick_grant|modal, sensitive_hit: true|false, simulate_ok: true|false, apply_latency_ms}. that'll let us measure safety.
li: +1. also log impacted_route_ids as a sampled list (PII safe) so we can correlate with routing changes later. sample at 1% by default.
ojobs-bot: (ops-bot) deploy: console/feature/quick-grant behind flag `quick_grant_kb` has been rolled to staging.
maya: thanks @ops-bot. quick note on API shape — proposing we use existing simulation endpoint and a small patch to grants API to support a `dry_run` + `apply_after_simulate=true` param so server can run both atomically and return a single outcome. example:```curl -X POST /authz/simulate -d '{"principal":"svc-123","roles":["viewer"]}'```then```PATCH /authz/grants/atomic {"principal":"svc-123","roles":["viewer"],"apply_after_simulate":true}```Thoughts?
sam: prefer server-side atomic operation to avoid race windows. exposing `apply_after_simulate` is fine but require a server-side check that simulation result is unchanged within 2s or fail.
jordan: also add an X-Requested-By header for console quick-grant so we can detect UI vs API automation in telemetry.
nora: tiny UX nit: keyboard hint should say "g — quick grant (press ⇧G for modal)" so power-users can opt into full flow explicitly. microcopy matters for admin trust.
li: test plan — create syrup test that exercises quick grant on: user role, service account, role with route_admin, role that touches quota overrides. verify telemetry + audit + no silent routing change.
maya: love it. i'll update prototype and PR with telemetry schema + server flag gating. leaving the thread open for any missed edge cases. :eyes:
sam: edge case: what about grants via quick-grant during ongoing rollout? if a canary is active we should prefer canary-safe roles or block. maybe simulation should include current rollout context.
jordan: yeah include rollout_context in simulate request, or simulate returns warnings if grant would bump traffic to blocked variant.
maya: ok adding rollout_context and a warning banner in UI if simulate warns. thanks everyone — will ping when PR is up for review.
